title: Dealing With High-Maintenance Team Members
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses the specific management challenge of a chronically needy team member whose demand for reassurance and attention is effectively bottomless. Using the memorable image of a cracked cup that never fills no matter how much a leader pours in, it explains why both ignoring the person and endlessly placating them make the problem worse. The prescribed approach is structured engagement: naming the disparity with how other team members operate, scheduling fixed check-in times rather than open-ended access, and directing some of the need toward outlets outside the team, including therapy in more extreme cases. It closes with practical, individualized plans, like written meeting recaps, as a way to convert vague neediness into a manageable, bounded process.
points: Both ignoring a needy team member and endlessly placating them tend to make the underlying neediness worse, not better.
Naming the disparity between the needy colleague and the rest of the team helps them understand why boundaries are being set.
Scheduling fixed, limited check-in times converts an open-ended demand for attention into a bounded, manageable process.
Directing some of the need toward outlets outside the team, including a therapist in extreme cases, is a legitimate part of the solution.
quotes: It's like these team members have a crack in the cup of self-confidence and personal validation.
Whatever the leader pours into the cup, it just leaks out of the crack, demanding even more time and attention with no end in sight.
Ignoring or limiting the time a leader gives the needy colleague typically makes the situation worse.
The best approach is to engage the needs of high maintenance colleague head-on without encouraging them.
Next, good leaders ask the high-maintenance team member to engage them at set times each week.
Leading a high-maintenance colleague is rarely fun or easy. But with a skillful appeal of setting clear boundaries, good leaders can help to repair a broken cup.
